original_title: Blizzard Reportedly Leads Xbox as 'Top-Performing' Studio Thanks to Overwatch and Diablo
summary_en: Leaked internal memos reveal Blizzard Entertainment has claimed the title of Microsoft's top-performing studio for FY26. This resurgence is largely credited to the continued success of **Overwatch** and the recent **Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred** expansion.

en.title: Blizzard Surges to Top Xbox Studio Thanks to Overwatch and Diablo 4
en.summary: Leaked internal memos reveal Blizzard Entertainment has claimed the title of Microsoft's top-performing studio for FY26. This resurgence is largely credited to the continued success of **Overwatch** and the recent **Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred** expansion.
en.body:
In a significant turnaround, **Blizzard Entertainment** has reportedly ascended to become the top-performing studio within the Xbox division for fiscal year 2026. This achievement, revealed through leaked internal communications, marks a new high point for the studio, driven primarily by the enduring popularity of **Overwatch** and the successful launch of **Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred**.

According to reports citing leaked emails from Blizzard president Johanna Faries, the studio concluded FY26 as the leading performer in Xbox's studios division. This period has been particularly fruitful, marking Blizzard's third-highest fiscal year for top-line revenue in its history. More impressively, FY25 and FY26 represent the first back-to-back years of growth for Blizzard since fiscal year 2017, a decade-long drought brought to an end by the strong performance of its key franchises.

> "In FY26 Blizzard ended the year as the top-performing studio in Xbox's studios division," Faries' leaked emails stated, "and this past year has marked our third highest fiscal for top line revenue in Blizzard's history."

While Blizzard oversees a portfolio of beloved IPs, the leaked communications specifically pointed to **Overwatch** and **Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred** as the primary engines of this exceptional performance. The second major expansion for **Diablo 4**, released in April of this year, introduced new story content, a fresh region, and sought-after classes like the Paladin and Warlock, building upon the game's established action-RPG foundation. Despite facing its share of controversies over the years, the **Diablo** franchise continues to be a powerhouse for the studio.

Meanwhile, **Overwatch**, despite its own fluctuations since its 2016 debut, has seen a renewed focus from Blizzard in recent years. The hero shooter underwent a significant reset in 2025 with the return of loot boxes and a new perk system. The momentum continued into 2026 with the rebranding of **Overwatch 2** back to **Overwatch**, accompanied by the addition of 10 new heroes, a move that evidently resonated strongly with players and contributed to its most robust quarter since 2022.

## A New Era for Blizzard Under Xbox

The implications of this internal success are substantial for both Blizzard and Microsoft. Coming on the heels of a less-than-stellar earnings report for Xbox overall, Blizzard's performance offers a much-needed boost and a clear indicator of where player engagement and revenue are currently strongest within the gaming giant's portfolio. This sustained growth, the first in nearly a decade, suggests that Blizzard's strategic decisions, including the revamping of **Overwatch** and the continued development of **Diablo 4**, are paying dividends.

## What This Means for Gamers

For the passionate global fanbase of **Overwatch** and **Diablo**, this news is a powerful affirmation. It signals that these core franchises are not only financially viable but are actively driving the success of one of gaming's most historic developers under new ownership. This increased investment and focus, evidenced by the revenue growth and the specific mention of **Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred** and **Overwatch**'s strong performance, suggests a bright future for ongoing content updates, new game development, and continued support for these beloved titles. The return to consecutive years of growth is a testament to the developers' dedication and the community's enduring loyalty.

## What's Next

While specific future projects beyond the ongoing support for **Overwatch** and **Diablo 4** have not been officially detailed, Blizzard's current trajectory indicates a strong commitment to its established franchises. Fans can anticipate continued content drops and potential expansions, with official announcements expected through Blizzard's own channels and Xbox's future gaming showcases.

content_raw: Blizzard Entertainment is reportedly Microsoft's golden child after Overwatch and Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred helped it become the "top-performing" Xbox studio. The World of Warcraft game developer's president, Johanna Faries, celebrated its status in leaked emails reported on by Windows Central . On the heels of a lackluster earnings report for Xbox, she was said to have told staff that Blizzard is firing on all cylinders. "In FY26 Blizzard ended the year as the top-performing studio in Xbox's studios division," Faries' leaked emails stated, "and this past year has marked our third highest fiscal for top line revenue in Blizzard's history." Blizzard's president then went on to confirm that FY25 and FY26 marked the studio's "first back-to-back years of growth since FY17." That's nearly 10 years without that kind of growth brought to an end thanks to two games in particular. Blizzard oversees a wealth of IP, but only two "drove exceptional performance" in particular: Overwatch and Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred. The latter, the second DLC expansion for 2023's Diablo 4 , launched in April of this year. It built upon its critically acclaimed action-RPG dungeon-crawler foundation with more story content, a new region, the Paladin and Warlock classes, and more. Through even its most controversial moments, Diablo remains one of Blizzard's strongest performers. Overwatch, meanwhile, has fluctuated in the 10 years since its launch, but recent years have shown the studio is willing to put the work into the hero shooter to not only keep it going but make it better than ever. The last two years have seen Blizzard deliver resets for Overwatch. It first began in 2025 with the return of loot boxes and the new perk system , while 2026 dropped the "2" to pick up the slack with 10 new heroes for the year and loads of quality-of-life updates. Was it all worth it? Faries seems to think so, with Overwatch recently boasting "its strongest quarter since 2022." Faries said its recent wins will help "shape Blizzard's future," which, for now, largely remains a mystery to the public. Windows Central also reported that the company is working on mobile spinoffs and trans-media projects for some of its franchises, while work on the next main Diablo project progresses. Although nothing has been officially announced, BlizzCon 2026 will hopefully offer a peek behind that curtain when it arrives September 12 – 13, 2026. "It's my hope that the event can shine a light on the work underway at Blizzard," the email continued, "and that it can serve as a powerful springboard into a new era of momentum and excitement behind our mission to bring joy and belonging for communities worldwide." Xbox, which also encompasses massive IPs like Call of Duty, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, Halo, and more, is otherwise going through a historic rough patch.
